0.headline: Crystal Crop Protection shares to list on Thursday; analysts recommend buy, sell or hold strategy
0.heading: Crystal Crop Protection shares to list on Thursday; analysts recommend buy, sell or hold strategy
0.intro: Rs 456-crore IPO was fully subscribed on the first day of bidding. The price band was fixed at Rs 259-272 per share.
0.body:
Crystal Crop Protection shares will be listed on the exchanges on Thursday, following a strong response to its initial public offering (IPO), which was subscribed 17 times during the November 18-20 bidding period.

Analysts expect the stock to list flat to up 10 percent over the upper end of the price band of Rs 272, advising long-term investors to consider holding the shares, while short-term investors may look at booking profits, if listing gains are available.

"We expect a listing that is flat to 10 percent above the upper band of Rs 272. Investors should look beyond listing gains and evaluate the stock from a medium-term perspective, as the integration of the acquisition could lead to a meaningful re-rating. Allottees with patience can hold through the integration phase, while others can look to accumulate on dips," said Sarvam Goel, Founder, Pocketful.

The Rs 456-crore IPO was fully subscribed on the first day of bidding. The price band was fixed at Rs 259-272 per share. The company had earlier raised Rs 136 crore from anchor investors.
Check All IPO News
Narendra Solanki, research analyst said investors with a long-term investment horizon may continue to hold the stock, considering the company's diversified portfolio and research and development (R&amp;D) capabilities. Short-term investors may consider booking profits from listing gains, he added.

Crystal Crop Protection is an R&amp;D-focused Indian agrochemical and agricultural solutions company with a diversified presence across crop protection products, natural crop solutions and seeds.

Its crop protection portfolio includes herbicides, fungicides, insecticides and technical-grade active ingredients. The natural crop solutions segment comprises bio-stimulants, bio-protectants, plant growth regulators, liquid fertilisers and micronutrients.

The company's seeds business offers field crop seeds, including cotton, mustard, pearl millet, sorghum, fodder crops, maize, wheat and rice, besides vegetable and flower seeds.

Solanki said the company follows an integrated business model covering product development, synthesis R&amp;D, seed breeding, manufacturing, regulatory registrations, brand building and distribution.

Its research capabilities are supported by the Key Research Development Centre (KRDC) at Sonipat in Haryana and nine field research stations. R&amp;D remains a key part of its growth strategy across the three business segments, supporting product innovation, portfolio expansion and long-term competitiveness.

At the upper end of the price band, the company is valued at a price-to-earnings multiple of 30.6 times its FY26 earnings, translating into a post-issue market capitalisation of approximately Rs 44,379 million, Solanki added. 

The company's portfolio includes more than 275 hybrid seed varieties, supported by 63 plant variety protection (PVP) registrations. Its revenue and profit after tax grew 16 percent and 22 percent, respectively, in FY26 over FY25.

"The proposed utilisation of Rs 247.94 crore towards debt repayment is expected to strengthen its balance sheet. Long-term investors may consider holding the shares, while short-term investors may book listing gains, if available," said Mahesh M Ojha, Vice-President, Research and Business Development, Kantilal Chhaganlal Securities Pvt Ltd.

1.headline: PhonePe resumes IPO process, likely to list in Q4 of FY 27 at $12-15 billion
1.heading: PhonePe resumes IPO process, likely to list in Q4 of FY 27 at $12-15 billion
1.intro: PhonePe is the country’s largest digital payments player with more than 45 percent market share in UPI payments.
1.body:
Walmart-owned PhonePe has resumed the Initial Public Offering (IPO) process and is looking to list at around $12-15 billion during Q4 of FY 27, according to bankers aware of the discussions.

The mobile payments major is likely to file the revised draft red herring prospectus in a fortnight, the sources added.

The company had paused the IPO process early this year, citing the geopolitical situation and investor sentiment.

As it happens, this comes on a day when there is wider tumult in another Walmart-owned company, Flipkart, whose CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy quit after a decade-long stint at the top, redefining the Indian e-commerce sector.

Interestingly, PhonePe was earlier part of the Flipkart Group before being hived off as a separate payments company.

PhonePe did not respond to Moneycontrol queries on the IPO process or potential valuation.

The offering is expected to raise around Rs 12,000 crore ( $1.3 billion) through a pure OFS or offer for sale, the sources added.

The company has been growing its topline by 40 percent with its credit business growing at 100 percent year over year, the bankers said.

According to one of the sources, PhonePe has managed to achieve net profitability during the first half of the current fiscal year, and this can help the company get a higher valuation compared to earlier expectations.

"PhonePe's revenue is likely to be higher than Paytm and the net profitability would help the company get a higher valuation than listed rival Paytm, which is now valued at around $11 billion," one of the bankers said.

Moneycontrol had reported that the company paused the IPO process as the mutual funds and other investment firms were not willing to give the company more than a $10 billion valuation.

PhonePe has reported an 11 percent increase in consolidated revenue for FY26 to Rs 7,920 crore, compared to Rs 7,115 crore it had reported in FY 25.

The company's consolidated net loss widened by 62 percent to Rs 2,792 crore in FY 26, compared to Rs 1,727 crore in FY 25.

PhonePe is the country’s largest digital payments player with more than 45 percent market share in UPI payments.

The company also has multiple other verticals, from a stock market trading app share.market, lending platform and sale of insurance policies, among others.
1.ai_impact_text_summary_s: Walmart-backed PhonePe resumed its IPO process, targeting a $12-15 billion valuation for Q4 FY27 and a $1.3 billion OFS. The profitable digital payments leader plans to file its draft prospectus soon, fueled by strong revenue and credit growth.

* Valuation projected between $12B and $15B.
* The firm achieved net profitability in H1 of the current fiscal.

2.headline: Matangi Rubber IPO to open on December 1, seeks valuation of Rs 492 crore
2.heading: Matangi Rubber IPO to open on December 1, seeks valuation of Rs 492 crore
2.intro: Matangi Rubber IPO | The company aims to raise Rs 125.16 crore through the IPO of 72.76 lakh shares and is seeking a valuation of Rs 492.2 crore at the upper end of the price band.
2.body:
Delhi-based tyre flaps and tubes manufacturer Matangi Rubber will launch its initial public offering (IPO) for public subscription on December 1, with a price band of Rs 163–172 per share.

The company aims to raise Rs 125.16 crore through the IPO of 72.76 lakh shares and is seeking a valuation of Rs 492.2 crore at the upper end of the price band.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of 57.61 lakh shares worth Rs 99.1 crore, while existing shareholders, including promoter Vandana Rubber and Chemicals, will offload 15.15 lakh shares worth Rs 26.06 crore through an offer for sale (OFS).

The company will open its one-day anchor book for institutional investors on November 30 and close the public issue on December 3. The IPO share allotment is expected to be finalised on December 4, while the company's shares are scheduled to list on the stock exchanges on December 8.

Of the total public issue, 50 percent has been reserved for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), 15 percent for non-institutional investors (NIIs) and the remaining 35 percent for retail investors.

Investors can bid for a minimum of 87 equity shares and in multiples of 87 shares thereafter. Accordingly, retail investors can make a minimum investment of Rs 14,964 for 87 shares and a maximum investment of Rs 1,94,532 for 1,131 shares.

Incorporated in 2004, Matangi Rubber operates five manufacturing plants. The company manufactures tyres for the two-wheeler and three-wheeler segments, while its tyre flaps and tubes are manufactured for commercial vehicles such as trucks, buses and heavy utility vehicles. Its rubber compounds are also used in the manufacturing of other rubber products.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

The company intends to utilise Rs 45 crore from the net proceeds of the fresh issue towards debt repayment, against total outstanding borrowings of Rs 97.56 crore as of June 2026.

Additionally, Rs 19.06 crore will be used to set up a greenfield manufacturing facility for rubber recycling products, while Rs 8.4 crore will be allocated towards establishing a greenfield manufacturing facility for solid tyre production in Bhind, Madhya Pradesh. The remaining proceeds will be utilised for general corporate purposes.

The company's tyre flaps contract manufacturing business contributed 73 percent to its revenue in FY26, while the manufacturing of tyres, tyre flaps and tubes on a job-work basis accounted for 21 percent.

On the financial front, Matangi Rubber's profit for the financial year ended March 2026 increased 11.5 percent to Rs 22.3 crore, while revenue grew 28.1 percent to Rs 129.8 crore compared with the previous financial year.

For the quarter ended June 2026, the company reported a profit of Rs 6.4 crore on revenue of Rs 47.7 crore.

Sarthi Capital Advisors has been appointed as the merchant banker managing the Matangi Rubber IPO.
